Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision at the
intersection in Pearland, Texas. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just give my name as the placeholder, if that's fine. I'm the driver of the vehicle that was hit on the driver's
side.
Q: That works for the file. Can you walk me through what happened leading up to the impact?
A: I was going through the intersection on a green light. I had slowed down a bit because traffic was backed up on the
cross street. Then a car came from my right and didn't stop for its red light. It hit the side of my car pretty hard.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the collision?
A: Only for a second. I glanced to the right and saw it coming, but there wasn't time to do anything except brace
myself.
Q: Where did you feel the impact, and were you able to get out of the vehicle on your own?
A: The impact was on my door, right where I was sitting. I was able to get out with some help from a bystander
because my left arm was hurting badly.
Q: Which injury are you most concerned about right now?
A: My right wrist. I fell against the steering wheel and then the door frame. The doctor said it's fractured, and they put
it in a splint. I'm giong to need to see a hand specialist next week.
Q: Have you received any medical treatment since the collision?
A: Yes, I went to the emergency room the same day, and I've had two follow-up visits since then. I've been keeping
the receipts and the discharge papers.
Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you would like to add to your statement?
A: Just that I was following the rules of the road and I want my car looked at as soon as possible. I'm not able to drive
it right now.
Q: Understood. Thank you for your cooperation. This conclueds the recorded statement.
</page>

it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
